content: Ritonavir can alter the metabolism of various drugs by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzymes, particularly CYP3A4 and CYP2D6, as well as transporters like P-glycoprotein (MDR1). Below are detailed interactions for each drug mentioned: 1. Tecovirimat: Tecovirimat decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely as tecovirimat is a weak CYP3A4 inducer. Adjust therapy if necessary. 2. Temsirolimus: Ritonavir increases temsirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for toxicity. 3. Teniposide: Ritonavir increases teniposide levels by inhibiting both CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein efflux. Monitor for adverse effects. 4. Tenofovir DF: Ritonavir increases tenofovir levels by reducing its elimination, raising the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely. 5. Terbinafine: Terbinafine increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, while ritonavir increases terbinafine levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 6. Tetrabenazine: Ritonavir enhances tetrabenazine effects by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Reduce tetrabenazine dose by 50% when co-administered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. 7. Tezacaftor: Ritonavir increases tezacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust tezacaftor dosage when co-administered with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 8. Theophylline: Ritonavir increases theophylline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for toxicity. 9. Tiagabine: Ritonavir increases tiagabine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 10. Ticagrelor: Ritonavir increases ticagrelor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A inhibitors. 11. Timolol: Ritonavir increases timolol levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism, potentially causing bradycardia, hypotension, and AV block. Consider lowering the beta-blocker dose. 12. Tinidazole: Ritonavir increases tinidazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 13. Tipranavir: Ritonavir increases tipranavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition, and both drugs raise the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely. 14. Tisotumab vedotin: Ritonavir increases tisotumab vedotin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially increasing systemic exposure to MMAE (active metabolite). Monitor for adverse effects. 15. Tobramycin: Ritonavir increases tobramycin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux. Monitor closely. 16. Tolterodine: Ritonavir increases tolterodine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 17. Tolvaptan: Ritonavir increases tolvaptan levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, and tolvaptan increases ritonavir levels similarly. Monitor closely. 18. Topiramate: Topiramate decreases ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 19. Toremifene: Ritonavir increases toremifene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for toxicity. 20. Tramadol: Ritonavir increases tramadol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, raising the risk of seizures and serotonin syndrome. Adjust tramadol dose or interval as needed. 21. Trazodone: Ritonavir increases trazodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while trazodone decreases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein. Monitor closely. 22. Triamcinolone acetonide: Ritonavir increases triamcinolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for systemic corticosteroid effects. 23. Triazolam: Ritonavir increases triazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 24. Trimipramine: Ritonavir increases trimipramine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Tucatinib: Tucatinib increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Consider reducing the dosage of P-glycoprotein substrates. 26. Ublituximab: Ublituximab reduces ritonavir effects due to immunosuppressive properties, increasing infection risk. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 27. Ubrogepant: Ritonavir decreases ubrogepant levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust ubrogepant dose as needed. 28. Ulipristal: Ritonavir increases ulipristal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 29. Umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol: Ritonavir increases levels of these drugs by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 30. Upadacitinib: Ritonavir increases upadacitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 31. Valbenazine: Ritonavir increases valbenazine levels by inhibiting both CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce valbenazine dose to 40 mg daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 32. Valsartan: Ritonavir increases valsartan levels by reducing hepatic clearance and inhibiting OATP1B1 and MRP2 transporters. Monitor for toxicity. 33. Vamorolone: Ritonavir increases vamorolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce vamorolone starting dose to 4 mg/kg/day, not exceeding 200 mg/day for patients over 50 kg. 34. Vardenafil: Ritonavir increases vardenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Adjust therapy and monitor closely. 35. Vemurafenib: Ritonavir increases vemurafenib levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition, and vemurafenib increases ritonavir levels similarly. Monitor closely. 36. Venlafaxine: Ritonavir increases venlafaxine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for toxicity. 37. Verapamil: Ritonavir increases verapamil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, while verapamil increases ritonavir levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor closely. 38. Viloxazine: Viloxazine increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Monitor and adjust doses of CYP2D6 substrates as needed. 39. Vinblastine: Ritonavir increases vinblastine levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor closely. 40. Vincristine: Ritonavir increases vincristine levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor closely. 41. Vincristine liposomal: Ritonavir increases vincristine liposomal levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Monitor closely. 42. Voclosporin: Ritonavir and voclosporin both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of arrhythmias. Monitor closely. 43. Warfarin: Ritonavir decreases warfarin levels by inducing CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Adjust warfarin dose and monitor INR closely. 44. Zafirlukast: Zafirlukast increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 45. Zanubrutinib: Ritonavir increases zanubrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce zanubrutinib dose to 80 mg daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 46. Zidovudine: Ritonavir and zidovudine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Monitor closely. 47. Zileuton: Ritonavir increases zileuton levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor for toxicity. 48. Zuranolone: Ritonavir increases zuranolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce zuranolone dose when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 49. Acetazolamide: Acetazolamide increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 50. Alfentanil: Ritonavir increases alfentanil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 51. Aliskiren: Ritonavir increases aliskiren levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein. Clinical significance is unknown. 52. Alosetron: Ritonavir increases alosetron levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 53. Alvimopan: Ritonavir increases alvimopan levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Clinical significance is unknown. 54. Amphetamine: Ritonavir increases amphetamine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 55. Anastrozole: Anastrozole increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 56. Aripiprazole: Ritonavir increases aripiprazole levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 57. Armodafinil: Ritonavir increases armodafinil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein. Clinical significance is unknown. 58. Atazanavir: Ritonavir increases atazanavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 59. Bosentan: Ritonavir increases bosentan levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 60. Cevimeline: Ritonavir increases cevimeline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 61. Chlorpromazine: Ritonavir increases chlorpromazine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 62. Clarithromycin: Ritonavir increases clarithromycin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 63. Cyclophosphamide: Cyclophosphamide increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 64. Dapsone: Ritonavir increases dapsone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 65. Dexfenfluramine: Ritonavir increases dexfenfluramine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 66. Dextroamphetamine: Ritonavir increases dextroamphetamine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 67. Dextromethorphan: Ritonavir increases dextromethorphan levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 68. Disopyramide: Ritonavir increases disopyramide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 69. Docetaxel: Ritonavir increases docetaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 70. Donepezil: Ritonavir increases donepezil levels by inhibiting both CYP2D6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 71. Drospirenone: Drospirenone increases ritonavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 72. Dutasteride: Ritonavir increases dutasteride levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 73. Efavirenz: Ritonavir increases efavirenz levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 74. Encainide: Ritonavir increases encainide levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 75. Eplerenone: Ritonavir increases eplerenone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 76. Eucalyptus: Ritonavir increases eucalyptus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown. 77. Fesoterodine: Ritonavir increases fesoterodine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Clinical significance is unknown.
